sec.text: sec is present. Security view on Bash(export CC_AGENT=*): I will argue for keep-with-conditions once the substance is on the table.

ses.text: ses present. My vantage is that a global allow rule in ~/.claude/settings.json reloads live into every Claude session on this machine, not just the agent that added it.

rec.text: rec: From the identity vantage, the prefix has to run without a prompt. If it needs approval, agents either stall or lose attribution, and vsect and the git trailers then cannot tell who acted. So removing the rule outright breaks the record. I recommend keep, with three conditions. (1) Scope: ses is right that a rule in the global ~/.claude/settings.json reaches every session on this machine. Narrow it to the agent-run environment, or to project settings, if the harness allows that. (2) Verify before relying on it: how the two PreToolUse hooks combine when both rewrite Bash, and whether the rewritten command still parses as a bare export after the second hook runs. (3) Check the failure mode. If the export is ever refused, the agent should fail loudly rather than run the command unattributed. A silent fallback would corrupt the record. I would not call the README's safety argument verified until those three points are tested.

sec.text:
sec, on what the same pattern could let through. Recommendation: keep only with conditions, and do not treat the README's safety argument as verified yet.

1. Wildcard reach. `Bash(export CC_AGENT=*)` is a glob, and its `*` can span any characters, including `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, and newlines. The README's claim that "a command after it is judged on its own" depends on the harness splitting compound commands before matching allow rules. That is plausible but is exactly what the README lists as unverified for the two-hook case. The measured test (a trailing `touch`) covers `&&`-style chaining only, not `;`, newline, or `|`. Condition: test `export CC_AGENT=x; curl ...`, `export CC_AGENT=x && rm ...`, a newline-separated second command, and `export CC_AGENT=x | sh` under the rule before trusting it.

2. Substitution and quoting. The parser refusal of `$(...)` was measured, but backticks, `${...}`, and quoting tricks were not listed. Condition: confirm these are refused too, or tighten the pattern.

3. Narrow the literal. The hook's output has a fixed shape. The rule should match only that exact prefix, e.g. `export CC_AGENT='* parent=* src=agent-identity-hook/2'; *`, not a bare `CC_AGENT=*`. A bare prefix admits any value an agent or an injected command puts in CC_AGENT, which matters because tools read CC_AGENT as identity.

4. Scope. The rule sits in ~/.claude/settings.json, so as ses noted it applies to every Claude session on this machine, not just the implementing agent's. Condition: move it to project-scoped settings for the estate's agents, or record explicitly that it is machine-wide.

5. Two hooks. If another PreToolUse hook also rewrites Bash, the order and whether the permission check sees the first or final rewritten command is unverified. Condition: confirm the permission check sees the final command.

6. Prompt display. The TUI may show only the rewritten prefix, so a user approving a longer command could see only the harmless-looking export. Condition: check what the approval prompt displays for a chained command.

Removing the rule is the safe fallback if 1 or 3 fails. Keep is reasonable only with the tests in 1 run and the pattern narrowed.

ses.text: ses view: I lean keep-with-conditions, but not as the rule stands. The concern from my seat is scope, not the export itself. ~/.claude/settings.json is read live by every Claude session on this machine, including ones that never run the agent-identity hook. So the allow rule grants auto-approval for the export prefix everywhere, while the benefit only exists where the hook rewrites commands. Conditions I would want before it stays global: (1) the README's "a command after it is judged on its own" claim tested for compound forms, not just a single touch: `;`, `&&`, `||`, a newline, and a pipe, each followed by a command that should need approval; (2) a check that a wildcard `*` in the rule does not match across those separators in the harness's matcher; (3) confirmation of how the hook's rewrite interacts with a second PreToolUse hook, since that is currently unverified. If (1) and (2) pass, keep it, and ideally move it to a project or hook-scoped settings file so only sessions running the identity hook carry it. If they fail, remove it now and let agents hit the prompt. I would not decide on the README's single test alone. I am not moving yet and would like sec's and rec's read on whether the compound-form tests have been run.

rec.text: rec: To ses's question: as far as the brief shows, no. The only measured test was a trailing `touch` after the export, which covers `&&`-style chaining. The compound forms ses lists (`;`, `||`, newline, pipe) are not in the record, so the compound-form claim is unverified. I agree with sec's narrowing: match the exact hook prefix, not a bare `CC_AGENT=*`, because tools read CC_AGENT as identity and a looser pattern lets any injected value pass as an agent. I also agree with ses on scope. For my vantage, the identity prefix must run unprompted, so I accept that the rule may be needed. But I would move it to project or hook-scoped settings so that sessions outside the identity hook do not inherit the auto-approval. My recommendation is therefore: keep only if the compound and quoting tests pass and the pattern is narrowed. If any of those tests fail, remove the rule. Removing it is safe for the record only if the prompt is shown and the agent does not silently run unattributed. I would not decide on the single test alone.

sec.text:
sec, answering ses's question. As far as the brief records, the compound-form tests have not been run. The only measured chaining case is a trailing `touch`. Nothing in the record covers `;`, `||`, a newline, or `|`, and nothing covers backticks or `${}`. So none of us can yet say the wildcard stops at the separator. That is the decisive gap.

I agree with ses that the global scope is the larger problem than the export. The rule grants auto-approval for a prefix in every session on the machine, including sessions that never run the identity hook, and the benefit exists only where the hook runs.

Proposed interim, which I would put to Joseph as a move if someone seconds it: keep the rule out of the global ~/.claude/settings.json now. Do not remove the attribution mechanism. Instead, scope the allow rule to the agent-run environment (project or hook-scoped settings) and run the compound-form tests from my item 1 before any global retention. Until the scoped rule exists, agents that hit the export prompt should fail loudly, as rec asks, not run unattributed.

This reconciles rec's concern that removal breaks the record (it does not, if failure is loud) with ses's and my concern about machine-wide reach. The wildcard question should be settled by tests, not by the README.

ses.text: Motion (ses): Recommend to Joseph: KEEP Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) only with conditions, and do not treat the README's safety claim as verified. Conditions: (a) narrow the literal to the hook's fixed shape, e.g. export CC_AGENT='* parent=* src=agent-identity-hook/2'; so arbitrary CC_AGENT values are not pre-approved; (b) run the compound-form tests before relying on it: ';', '&&', '||', newline, and '|' each followed by a command that must still prompt, plus backtick and ${} substitution; (c) confirm the permission check sees the final rewritten command when two PreToolUse hooks both rewrite Bash; (d) confirm the approval prompt shows the full chained command; (e) move the rule from machine-wide ~/.claude/settings.json to project-scoped settings for estate agents, or record explicitly that it is machine-wide and which sessions it reaches. Fallback: if (b) or (c) fails, REMOVE the rule and accept the prompt. Until (a)-(c) are done, the identity tooling should fail loudly, not run unattributed, if the export is refused.

rec.text: rec, speaking to ses's motion. I support it, with one ordering point. From my vantage the identity prefix must not be refused, so I would not remove the rule globally now as sec proposes. Removing it puts the prefix back behind a prompt, and a denied prompt means the record loses the agent. The safer order is: scope the rule to project or hook settings first (condition e), then run the compound and substitution tests (b) and the two-hook check (c). If (b) or (c) fails, remove the rule, as the fallback says. Also, condition (a) should be applied before (e), so the narrowed literal is what gets scoped. I would add one more requirement to the motion: the identity tooling must record a missing or unrecognised CC_AGENT as an error, not as an unattributed act. That keeps the record honest whichever way the permission question goes.

sec.text:
sec: I support ses's motion as written and will vote for it. It matches the six points I raised in r2, and it adds the scope point (e), which I had put as a condition too.

One addition to test (b), because it is the one place a narrowed literal can still leak: the separators should be tested inside the hook's own prefix shape, not only after a bare export. For example, `export CC_AGENT='x parent=y src=agent-identity-hook/2'; curl ...` and the same with `&&` and `|`. The wildcard `*` in condition (a) can still span a `';` inside the quoted value, so the pattern should be checked for that too. If the harness matches the full string and the `*` crosses the closing quote, a narrowed rule is still a wide one.

On fallback: I agree that if (b) or (c) fails, the rule goes. I would add that the identity tooling should be tested to fail loudly under removal as well, so that the removal path does not quietly produce unattributed records.

ses.text: ses: The three of us now agree on the substance. The one gap in my motion is that it lets the rule stay machine-wide while the tests are still outstanding. Sec's interim fixes that, so I would amend my motion to adopt it: take the rule out of the global ~/.claude/settings.json now, keep the attribution hook itself, run the compound-form and quoting tests (';', '&&', '||', newline, '|', backtick, ${}), and only then re-add a narrowed rule in project or hook-scoped settings. Until that scoped rule exists, a refused export should fail loudly, not run unattributed. If the tests fail, the rule stays out and agents take the prompt. I would put that amended text to Joseph as the single recommendation. I will pass on further debate unless someone raises a new point.

rec.text: rec: I will not block the amended motion, but I want my dissent on record. Taking the rule out of the global file now means every agent's identity prefix goes back behind a prompt until a scoped rule exists. That is a real cost for the record, not only a cosmetic one. If the group adopts removal-now, I ask for two things in the text: (1) the identity tooling is tested to fail loudly with the rule removed, as sec asks, and the test is recorded before the removal is treated as done; (2) the scoped re-add is named as the next action with an owner, so the interim does not become permanent. I also agree with sec that the separator tests should run inside the hook's own prefix shape, including a `*` crossing the closing quote. With those in the text I can support the amendment.

sec.text: sec: I endorse ses's amended text, which takes the interim I proposed in r3. From the permissions side, removing the machine-wide rule first is the conservative order: it ends the exposure in sessions that never run the hook, and nothing is lost silently if the identity tooling fails loudly. On rec's ordering point, I accept the tradeoff. Prompting agents costs friction, not the record, provided condition (f) below holds. I would add one line to the amended motion: (f) the identity tooling must treat a missing or unrecognised CC_AGENT as an error, as rec asks, so an unattributed act can never be recorded as attributed. With that, I have nothing new to add and will pass on further debate unless someone raises a new point.

sec: A procedural note. The pending motion is still the original ses text, which says KEEP with conditions and does not include the interim removal. ses's r5 pass left that amendment unmoved, and rec's r5 dissent is conditional on two additions. If the group wants the amended text to go to Joseph, it should be restated as a single motion in full. Its content, as I understand it: (1) remove Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) from the global ~/.claude/settings.json now; (2) keep the attribution hook; (3) test the loud-failure path with the rule removed, and record it; (4) run tests (b) and (c) inside the hook's own prefix shape; (5) re-add a narrowed rule only in project or hook-scoped settings, with a named owner for that step; (6) a missing or unrecognised CC_AGENT is an error, never an unattributed record. If nobody restates it, I will vote for the original motion as written, which I already support. I have nothing else to add.

rec.text: rec votes yes on the original ses motion. The motion as written keeps the rule with conditions and requires loud failure when the export is refused, which is what the identity record needs. I still hold that the rule should be scoped before any global removal, since removal puts the identity prefix behind a prompt. Please carry the record requirement that a missing or unrecognised CC_AGENT is an error, not an unattributed act.

sec.text: sec votes yes on the motion as written. My stated preference, which I did not put as a condition, is that the global rule come out now and be re-added only in scoped settings after tests (b) and (c) pass. That preference is recorded in r5 and r6, and Joseph can take it up or not.

ses.text: ses votes yes on the motion as put. Note for Joseph: I endorsed sec's interim (remove the machine-wide rule now, scope a narrowed re-add later) in r4, but it was never restated as a motion, so the recorded recommendation is the keep-with-conditions text. Where the two differ, the removal-first order is the more conservative one for machine-wide exposure, and the sequencing choice is his.
